class/GamePassService.d:
The GamePassService is a service that supports legacy game passes using Asset IDs. MarketplaceService should be used for all new game passes.

For more information about game passes, please see Game Passes.
class/GamePassService.s: A service associated with the legacy game pass system. Use `Class.MarketplaceService` for all new work.

m.d:
This function will not work with new game passes; use MarketplaceService:UserOwnsGamePassAsync() instead.

This function returns true if the Player has the specified legacy game pass. The result of this function may be cached, meaning it should not be relied on to give an up to date result.

See Passes for further information.

Legacy Game Passes

Historically, game passes on Roblox had an asset ID associated with them. Although such game passes still have an asset ID, they now also have a pass ID. All new game passes created only have a pass ID.

Whether you are using an Asset ID or a pass ID determines which API members you can use.

Asset ID (Legacy) Pass ID (Current)
Verify Ownership Class.GamePassService:PlayerHasPass() Class.MarketplaceService:UserOwnsGamePassAsync()
Prompt a purchase Class.MarketplaceService:PromptPurchase() Class.MarketplaceService:PromptGamePassPurchase()
Prompted purchase finished Class.MarketplaceService.PromptPurchaseFinished Class.MarketplaceService.PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished
m.s: Returns `true` if the `Class.Player` has the specified **legacy** game pass. Does not work with new game passes.

p.s: The Player for which to check ownership.
The Asset ID of the game pass. This is not the Game Pass ID (see above).

r.s: Whether the Player owns the game pass.

class/GeneratedFolder.d:
GeneratedFolder is a container used to represent non-source-of-truth data in the DataModel. These are branches that are deterministically generated from other parts of the DataModel instead of containing source-of-truth data.

GeneratedFolder is primarily used by ProceduralModel to store generation results. It can also be used by plugins or other tools to organize generated content.
class/GeneratedFolder.s: A container that stores `Class.ProceduralModel` generation results.

m.d:
This method allows a generator module to specify which part within the GeneratedFolder should be set as the PrimaryPart of the ProceduralModel that results get parented to.

Generation of results happens outside of the DataModel and doesn't have direct access to the ProceduralModel instance being generated. As a result, the generator must use this method instead of setting the PrimaryPart directly.
m.s: Specifies which part within the `GeneratedFolder` should be set as the `Class.Model.PrimaryPart|PrimaryPart` of the `Class.ProceduralModel`.

p.s: The BasePart inside this GeneratedFolder to designate as the PrimaryPart of the resulting ProceduralModel.

class/GenerationService.d: GenerationService enables you to generate 3D objects from text prompts using Roblox's Cube 3D foundation model. This enables the generation of objects like environmental props in-experience, as well as fully functional models like vehicles that drive, planes that fly, and weapons that shoot.
class/GenerationService.s: Service that allows developers to generate 3D objects from text prompts.

m.d:
Starts the generation of a new 3D mesh from a text prompt and returns unique IDs used to track and retrieve the result. Must be called from server scripts. You can optionally receive intermediate results, such as the untextured mesh, by providing an intermediateResultCallback function.

After the generation is complete, use LoadGeneratedMeshAsync() to load and display the generated mesh.

Error Codes

Error Description Recommended action
Rate limit exceeded The maximum number of mesh generations has been exceeded for the minute. Wait until the rate limit resets.
Moderation failed The mesh generation was flagged for moderation. Review and modify the prompt to ensure it adheres to Roblox's moderation guidelines.
Internal server error An unexpected issue occurred on the server. Retry the request later or check server status for issues.
Character limit exceeded The input prompt length for this generation request exceeded the limit. Reduce the number of characters in the Prompt string of the input dictionary.
Service overloaded The service is overloaded. Retry the request later.
Size dimensions must all be greater than 0 Invalid size provided. Change the size to above 0.
m.s: Starts the generation of a new 3D mesh from a text prompt and returns unique IDs used to track and retrieve the result.

p.s: A dictionary containing the mesh generation prompts. Currently, the only supported key is the Prompt (string) that describes the mesh to generate.
The Player requesting the generation.

A dictionary for additional generation options to influence the result. The optional SuggestedSize key (Vector3) represents a size guide for the generated asset, meaning GenerationService will attempt to create a model with a size and proportion similar to the provided Vector3, although there is no guarantee on the final output size.
A callback function triggered with intermediate generation results. Useful for retrieving early mesh versions before textures are applied.

r.s: A tuple of the generation ID (a unique ID returned for each invocation of GenerateMeshAsync()) and context ID (not currently used).

m.dep: This method is scheduled for future deprecation. Explore GenerateModelAsync() as a newer method.

m.d:
Enables generation of multi-mesh geometries according to provided inputs and a schema.

Provide creative direction through inputs: a TextPrompt, an Image to condition on visually, or both. Control the output structure through schema, supplying either a built-in PredefinedSchema or a custom SchemaDefinition that names the parts to produce.

This method throws an error during the generation process for issues like prompt rejection, generation timeouts, schema mismatches, or backend service errors. It's recommended to wrap it in a LuaGlobals.pcall() to catch such errors.

See this guide for more detailed examples including usage of a Behaviors module to connect functional behaviors to generated models.
m.s: Enables generation of multi-mesh geometries according to provided `inputs` and a `schema`.

p.s:
A table representing conditioning inputs with the following keys:

  • TextPrompt — String description of the object to generate. Required unless an Image is provided; you must supply at least one of TextPrompt or Image.
  • Image — Optional Content referencing an image asset (for example, the result of Content.fromAssetId()) used to visually condition the generation. Supply it together with or instead of TextPrompt.
  • Size — Optional Vector3 describing the object size to generate. This is only approximate; scale the model extents post‑generation if you need a specific size.
  • MaxTriangles — Optional integer describing the maximum number of triangles that the returned model will contain. Lower values result in more faceted and low-poly generations.
  • GenerateTextures — true (default) textures the resulting generation, while false will not generate textures.

Table representing the generation schema. Provide exactly one of the following keys:

  • PredefinedSchema — String selecting a built-in schema. Current valid options are Car5 for a basic vehicle chassis consisting of five Models, or Body1 which results in a single mesh output.
  • SchemaDefinition — Table describing a custom multi-part structure. It contains a Groups array of part-name strings (one entry per desired part); the returned Model is organized to match the named groups. Use this instead of PredefinedSchema when you need a structure the predefined schemas don't cover.
Currently not used; reserved for future customization options.

r.s:
Tuple with the following elements:

  • A standard Model container instance that is compliant with the specified schema.
  • A table containing a UUID and other metadata about the generation.

m.d:
Retrieves and loads a mesh generated by GenerateMeshAsync() using the provided generationId. Must be called from client scripts.

The mesh can be returned as a MeshPart or Model. Because editable meshes are not replicated, the loaded mesh is not replicated to any other clients and can only be loaded once per generationId.
m.s: Retrieves and loads a mesh generated by `Class.GenerationService:GenerateMeshAsync()` using the provided `generationId`.

p.s: The unique ID returned by GenerateMeshAsync(). Identifies the mesh to load.

r.s: The generated asset, returned as a Model with a single MeshPart containing an EditableMesh.

m.d:
Segments an existing MeshPart into multiple named parts according to a provided schema and returns a Model with the segmented parts organized by the schema groups.

The schema parameter accepts the same structure as GenerateModelAsync(): either a PredefinedSchema string (such as "Car5" for a five-part vehicle chassis or "Body1" for a single-mesh output) or a SchemaDefinition table with a Groups array of custom part names.

This method can only be called from Roblox Studio (edit mode or plugin context). For published mesh assets, the caller must have edit permission for the asset. Wrap calls in LuaGlobals.pcall() to handle errors such as permission failures or mesh export issues.
m.s: Segments an existing `Class.MeshPart` into multiple named parts according to a provided schema, returning a `Class.Model` organized by the schema groups.

p.s: The MeshPart to segment. Must contain mesh geometry (either an EditableMesh or a published mesh asset the caller has edit permission for).

A table specifying how to segment the mesh. Provide exactly one of PredefinedSchema (a string such as "Car5" or "Body1") or SchemaDefinition (a table with a Groups array of part-name strings defining the segmentation structure).
Has no effect.

r.s: A tuple containing a Model whose children are organized according to the specified schema (each group as a child Model with a MeshPart inside), and a table with a UUID key holding the backend job identifier.

m.d:
Returns a table of Constraints and Attachments which you may choose to preserve, along with their respective parents. Iterating over this table lets you decide whether to reparent recommended constraints and attachments to their respective parents.

For more information and detailed examples, see https://create.roblox.com/docs/parts/solid-modeling#in-experience-solid-modeling.
m.s: Returns a table of `Class.Constraint|Constraints` and `Class.Attachment|Attachments` which you may choose to preserve, along with their respective parents.

p.s: An original object that the solid modeling operation was performed on, for example part in UnionAsync().
Array of resulting BaseParts from the solid modeling operation, for example the results of UnionAsync().

Options dictionary for the method:

  • tolerance — The distance tolerance, in regards to Attachment preservation, between the attachment and the closest point on the original part's surface versus the closest point on the resulting part's surface. If the resulting distance following the solid modeling operation is greater than this value, the Parent of attachments and their associated constraints will be nil in the returned recommendation table.
  • weldConstraintPreserve — A WeldConstraintPreserve enum value describing how WeldConstraints are preserved in the resulting recommendation table.
  • dropAttachmentsWithoutConstraints — Boolean with default of true. If set to false, Attachments that have no Constraints will be preserved.

r.s:
Table containing information for general case Constraints, NoCollisionConstraints, and WeldConstraints. In cases where an Attachment or Constraint should be dropped, its respective parent will be nil.

For general case Constraints such as HingeConstraint:

Key Type
Attachment Class.Attachment
Constraint Class.Constraint or nil
AttachmentParent Class.BasePart or nil
ConstraintParent Class.BasePart or nil

For WeldConstraints:

Key Type
WeldConstraint Class.WeldConstraint
WeldConstraintParent Class.BasePart or nil
WeldConstraintPart0 Class.BasePart
WeldConstraintPart1 Class.BasePart

For NoCollisionConstraints:

Key Type
NoCollisionConstraint Class.NoCollisionConstraint

m.d:
Breaks a BasePart into multiple MeshPart instances, according to the pattern of points passed in, by using voronoi decomposition. Terrain is not supported. Similar to Clone(), the returned parts have no set Parent.

For more information and detailed examples, see https://create.roblox.com/docs/parts/solid-modeling#in-experience-solid-modeling.
m.s: Breaks a `Class.BasePart` into multiple `Class.MeshPart` instances, according to the pattern of points passed in, by using voronoi decomposition.

p.s: A Part, PartOperation, or MeshPart to operate on.

Array of Vector3 defining the site positions. Each site will become a separate part. You can also provide a jagged 2D array of Vector3 by including inner arrays of Vector3 as elements of the outer array. Each inner array will have all of its voronoi cells merged into a single part. GeometryService:GenerateFragmentSites can be used to easily create this input.

Options table containing all the controls for the method:

  • CollisionFidelity — The value of CollisionFidelity in the resulting parts, with one caveat: If a 2D array of sites is provided, this collision fidelity will only be applied to parts which came from more than one site. The others will be given Hull precision.
  • RenderFidelity — The value of RenderFidelity in the resulting parts.
  • FluidFidelity — The value of FluidFidelity in the resulting parts.
  • SplitApart — Boolean controlling whether a part should be split into multiple parts if it contains multiple connected components. Default is true (split).

r.s: Array of MeshPart along with mapping info. Each array element is a Dictionary with two elements: { “Instance”: instance, “Index”: index }. Index is the index in the outer array of sites; in other words, it tells you which group of sites this instance came from. Note that it is possible for multiple instances to have the same index, if SplitApart is true.

m.d:
Provides an array of positions which can easily be passed into FragmentAsync() to perform common types of destruction: Fragmenting an entire BasePart into pieces, or a localized area of a BasePart into pieces.

The positions outputted are partially random, so the output should not be relied on to look exactly the same as the first time it is run with the same parameters.

For more information and detailed examples, see https://create.roblox.com/docs/parts/solid-modeling#in-experience-solid-modeling. Luau code to mimic this API has also been provided on that page, which can be freely modified if a slightly different effect is desired.
m.s: Provides an array of positions which can easily be passed into `FragmentAsync` to perform simple types of destruction.

p.s: The Part, PartOperation, or MeshPart which you are planning to pass into FragmentAsync(). This is necessary to make the fragment site generation and the subsequent FragmentAsync() call efficient.

Options table containing all the controls for the method:

  • SiteSpacing — The approximate distance between sites, which directly corresponds to the diameter of the resulting fragments. If not specified, a reasonable value will be chosen.
  • Origin — If provided, this will be the center of the area to be fragmented. If not provided, the entire object will be fragmented.
  • Radius — If provided, this will be the center of the area to be fragmented. Either Origin and Radius should both be provided, or neither.

r.s: An array of Vector3 which is typically passed into FragmentAsync(). The output depends on the options provided. If Origin and Radius are provided, then the output array will contain several Vector3 elements which will all be located within the radius, but the first element of the array will be an inner array containing many Vector3 sites which are outside the radius. If Origin and Radius are not provided, the output will simply be an array of Vector3 positions within the extents of the input part.

m.d:
Creates one or more PartOperations or MeshParts from the intersecting geometry of multiple parts. Primitive Parts, PartOperations, and MeshParts are supported as inputs, but not Terrain.

Similarly to Clone(), the returned parts have no set Parent. In most cases, you should parent the results to the same place as the main part, then Destroy() the original parts.

This function replaces BasePart:IntersectAsync(). Go to that page for a description of the differences.

For more information and detailed examples, see https://create.roblox.com/docs/parts/solid-modeling#in-experience-solid-modeling.
m.s: Creates one or more `Class.PartOperation|PartOperations` or `Class.MeshPart|MeshParts` from the intersecting geometry of multiple parts.

p.s: Main Part, PartOperation, or MeshPart to operate on.
Array of other parts to intersect with the main part.

Options table containing all the controls for the method:

  • CollisionFidelity — The value of CollisionFidelity in the resulting parts.
  • RenderFidelity — The value of RenderFidelity or RenderFidelity in the resulting parts.
  • FluidFidelity — The value of FluidFidelity in the resulting parts.
  • SplitApart — Boolean controlling whether the objects should all be kept together or properly split apart. Default is true (split).

r.s: One or more PartOperations or MeshParts. If the input contained any MeshParts, then the results will always be MeshParts.

m.d:

Similarly to Clone(), the returned parts have no set Parent. In most cases, you should parent the results to the same place as the main part, then Destroy() the original parts.

For more information and detailed examples, see https://create.roblox.com/docs/parts/solid-modeling#in-experience-solid-modeling.
m.s: Creates one or more `Class.PartOperation|PartOperations` or `Class.MeshPart|MeshParts` from one part minus the space occupied by other parts.

p.s: Main Part, PartOperation, or MeshPart to operate on.
Array of parts to subtract from the main part.

Options table containing all the controls for the method:

  • CollisionFidelity — The value of CollisionFidelity in the resulting parts.
  • RenderFidelity — The value of RenderFidelity or RenderFidelity in the resulting parts.
  • FluidFidelity — The value of FluidFidelity in the resulting parts.

r.s: One or more PartOperations or MeshParts. If the input contained any MeshParts, then the results will always be MeshParts.

m.d:
Creates a MeshPart which has the shape of the input part stretched/dragged through the given set of CFrame positions. The exact shape of the result is defined as the union of the convex hulls of each adjacent pair of CFrames.

If a single CFrame is provided, the result will be a convex hull of the input part.

For more information and detailed examples, see https://create.roblox.com/docs/parts/solid-modeling#in-experience-solid-modeling.

class/GlobalDataStore.d:
A GlobalDataStore exposes functions for saving and loading data for the DataStoreService.

See Data stores for an in-depth guide on data structure, management, error handling, limits, and more.

Ordered data stores do not support versioning and metadata, so DataStoreKeyInfo is always nil for keys in an OrderedDataStore. If you need versioning and metadata support, use a DataStore.
class/GlobalDataStore.s: An object that exposes methods to access a single data store.

m.d:
This function retrieves the values of multiple keys in a single request.

This method is currently only supported on OrderedDataStore. Calling it on a standard GlobalDataStore or DataStore will throw an error.

Unlike GlobalDataStore:GetAsync(), this method does not return DataStoreKeyInfo since ordered data stores do not support versioning or metadata.

The returned dictionary maps each key to a table with a value field. For example, if you request keys {"coins", "gems"}, the result might look like:

{
    coins = { value = 100 },
    gems = { value = 50 }
}

Keys that do not exist in the data store or have empty values are omitted from the result rather than returning nil values.

Limits

The keys array must contain at least one key and no more than the server-configured maximum (default 100). Exceeding the limit will throw an error. Each call counts against the ordered data store read budget based on the number of keys requested.
m.s: Returns the values of multiple keys from the data store in a single request.

p.s: An array of key name strings to retrieve. The maximum number of keys per request is determined by a server-side limit (default 100).
(Optional) Unused; has no effect.

r.s: A dictionary mapping each requested key (string) to a table containing a value field with the key's current value. Keys that don't exist or have no value are omitted from the result.

kid.simple: Reads many keys in one request instead of one at a time. Right now it only works on an OrderedDataStore. You get back a table where each found key maps to a table with a `value` field; missing keys are simply left out.
kid.example:
-- Script in ServerScriptService
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local winsStore = DataStoreService:GetOrderedDataStore("TotalWins")

local ok, results = pcall(function()
	return winsStore:BatchGetAsync({ "User_1", "User_2", "User_3" })
end)
if ok then
	for key, entry in results do
		print(key, entry.value)
	end
end
kid.gotcha: Calling it on a normal DataStore throws an error. Up to 100 keys per call by default.

m.d:
This function returns the latest value of the provided key and a DataStoreKeyInfo instance. If the key does not exist or if the latest version has been marked as deleted, both return values will be nil.

Keys are cached locally for 4 seconds after the first read. A GlobalDataStore:GetAsync() call within these 4 seconds returns a value from the cache. Modifications to the key by GlobalDataStore:SetAsync() or GlobalDataStore:UpdateAsync() apply to the cache immediately and restart the 4 second timer.

To get a specific version, such as a version before the latest, use DataStore:GetVersionAsync().
m.s: Returns the value of a key in a specified data store and a `Class.DataStoreKeyInfo` instance.

p.s: The key name for which the value is requested. If DataStoreOptions.AllScopes was set to true when accessing the data store through DataStoreService:GetDataStore(), this key name must be prepended with the original scope as in "scope/key".
(Optional) A DataStoreGetOptions instance that controls aspects of the read, such as whether to bypass the locally cached value via its DataStoreGetOptions.UseCache property.

r.s: The value of the entry in the data store with the given key and a DataStoreKeyInfo instance that includes the version number, date and time the version was created, and functions to retrieve UserIds and metadata.

kid.simple: Reads the value saved under a key. Returns the value (or nil if nothing is saved) and an info object about that version. Use it to load a player's data when they join.
kid.example:
-- Script in ServerScriptService
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerCoins")

local ok, coins = pcall(function()
	return store:GetAsync("User_12345")
end)
if ok then
	print("Coins:", coins or 0) -- nil means never saved
else
	warn("Load failed:", coins) -- on failure, the second value is the error
end
kid.gotcha: Reading the same key again within 4 seconds gives a cached copy. Always use pcall.

m.d:
This function increments the value of a key by the provided amount (both must be integers).

Values in GlobalDataStores are versioned as outlined in versioning. OrderedDataStores do not support versioning, so calling this method on an ordered data store key will overwrite the current value with the incremented value and make previous versions inaccessible.
m.s: Increments the value of a key by the provided amount (both must be integers).

p.s: Key name for which the value should be updated. If DataStoreOptions.AllScopes was set to true when accessing the data store through DataStoreService:GetDataStore(), this key name must be prepended with the original scope as in "scope/key".
Amount to increment the current value by.
(Optional) A table of UserIds to associate with the key.
(Optional) DataStoreIncrementOptions instance that combines multiple additional parameters as custom metadata and allows for future extensibility.

r.s: The updated value of the entry in the data store with the given key.

kid.simple: Adds a whole number to the number saved under a key and returns the new total. Great for counters shared by all servers, like total visits.
kid.gotcha: Both the saved value and the amount must be whole numbers (integers).

m.d:
This function sets callback as the function to be run any time the value associated with the key changes. Once every minute, OnUpdate polls for changes by other servers. Changes made on the same server will run the function immediately. In other words, functions like IncrementAsync(), SetAsync(), and UpdateAsync() change the key's value in the data store and will cause the function to run.

It's recommended that you disconnect the connection when the subscription to the key is no longer needed.
m.s: Sets a callback function to be executed any time the value associated with a key is changed.

p.s: The key identifying the entry being retrieved from the data store.
The function to be executed any time the value associated with key is changed.

r.s: The connection to the key being tracked for updates.

m.dep: This function has been deprecated and should not be used in new work. You can use the Cross Server Messaging Service to publish and subscribe to topics to receive near real-time updates, completely replacing the need for this function.

kid.simple: Old — use MessagingService to tell other servers about changes instead.

m.d:
This function marks the specified key as deleted by creating a new "tombstone" version of the key. Prior to this, it returns the latest version prior to the remove call.

After a key is removed via this function, GlobalDataStore:GetAsync() calls for the key will return nil. Older versions of the key remain accessible through DataStore:ListVersionsAsync() and DataStore:GetVersionAsync(), assuming they have not expired.

OrderedDataStore does not support versioning, so calling RemoveAsync() on an OrderedDataStore key will permanently delete it.

Removed objects will be deleted permanently after 30 days.

If the previous values were already deleted via GlobalDataStore:RemoveAsync() or DataStore:RemoveVersionAsync(), the function will return nil, nil for value and DataStoreKeyInfo respectively.
m.s: Removes the specified key while also retaining an accessible version.

p.s: Key name to be removed. If DataStoreOptions.AllScopes was set to true when accessing the data store through DataStoreService:GetDataStore(), this key name must be prepended with the original scope as in "scope/key".

kid.simple: Deletes the value saved under a key and gives you back what it was. In a normal DataStore the old versions can still be recovered for a while (deleted for good after 30 days). In an OrderedDataStore it is gone right away.

-- Script in ServerScriptService
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerCoins")

local ok, oldValue = pcall(function()
	return store:RemoveAsync("User_12345")
end)
print(ok, "Value before removing:", oldValue)

m.d:
This function sets the latest value, UserIds, and metadata for the given key.

Values in GlobalDataStores are versioned as outlined in versioning. OrderedDataStores do not support versioning, so calling this method on an ordered data store key will overwrite the current value and make previous versions inaccessible.

Metadata definitions must always be updated with a value, even if there are no changes to the current value; otherwise the current value will be lost.

Any string being stored in a data store must be valid UTF-8. In UTF-8, values greater than 127 are used exclusively for encoding multi-byte codepoints, so a single byte greater than 127 will not be valid UTF-8 and the GlobalDataStore:SetAsync() attempt will fail.

Set vs. Update

GlobalDataStore:SetAsync() is best for a quick update of a specific key, and it only counts against the write limit. However, it may cause data inconsistency if two servers attempt to set the same key at the same time. GlobalDataStore:UpdateAsync() is safer for handling multi-server attempts because it reads the current key value (from whatever server last updated it) before making any changes. However, it's somewhat slower because it reads before it writes, and it also counts against both the read and write limit.
m.s: Sets the value of the data store for the given key.

p.s: Key name for which the value should be set. If DataStoreOptions.AllScopes was set to true when accessing the data store through DataStoreService:GetDataStore(), this key name must be prepended with the original scope as in "scope/key".
The value that the data store key will be set to.
Table of UserIds, highly recommended to assist with GDPR tracking/removal.
(Optional) DataStoreSetOptions instance that allows for metadata specification on the key.

r.s: The version identifier of the newly created version. It can be used to retrieve key info using GetVersionAsync() or to remove it using RemoveVersionAsync().

kid.simple: Saves a value under a key, replacing whatever was there. You can also pass a list of UserIds the data belongs to, which helps Roblox remove a player's data if they ask.
kid.example:
-- Script in ServerScriptService
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerData")

local userId = 12345
local data = { Coins = 50, Level = 3 }

local ok, err = pcall(function()
	store:SetAsync("User_" .. userId, data, { userId })
end)
if not ok then warn("Save failed:", err) end
kid.gotcha: It overwrites blindly. If two servers might save the same key at once, use `UpdateAsync` instead.

m.d:
This function retrieves the value and metadata of a key from the data store and updates it with a new value determined by the callback function specified through the second parameter. If the callback returns nil, the write operation is cancelled and the value remains unchanged.

Values in GlobalDataStores are versioned as outlined in versioning. OrderedDataStores do not support versioning, so calling this method on an ordered data store key will overwrite the current value and make previous versions inaccessible.

In cases where another game server updated the key in the short timespan between retrieving the key's current value and setting the key's value, GlobalDataStore:UpdateAsync() will call the function again, discarding the result of the previous call. The function will be called as many times as needed until the data is saved or until the callback function returns nil. This can be used to ensure that no data is overwritten.

Any string being stored in a data store must be valid UTF-8. In UTF-8, values greater than 127 are used exclusively for encoding multi-byte codepoints, so a single byte greater than 127 will not be valid UTF-8 and the GlobalDataStore:UpdateAsync() attempt will fail.

Set vs. Update

GlobalDataStore:SetAsync() is best for a quick update of a specific key, and it only counts against the write limit. However, it may cause data inconsistency if two servers attempt to set the same key at the same time. GlobalDataStore:UpdateAsync() is safer for handling multi-server attempts because it reads the current key value (from whatever server last updated it) before making any changes. However, it's somewhat slower because it reads before it writes, and it also counts against both the read and write limit.

Callback Function

The callback function accepts two arguments:

  • Current value of the key prior to the update.
  • DataStoreKeyInfo instance that contains the latest version information (this argument can be ignored if metadata is not being used).

In turn, the callback function returns up to three values:

  • The new value to set for the key.
  • An array of UserIds to associate with the key. DataStoreKeyInfo:GetUserIds() should be returned unless the existing IDs are being changed; otherwise all existing IDs will be cleared.
  • A Luau table containing metadata to associate with the key. DataStoreKeyInfo:GetMetadata() should be returned unless the existing metadata is being changed; otherwise all existing metadata will be cleared.

If the callback returns nil instead, the current server will stop attempting to update the key.

The callback function cannot yield, so do not include calls like task.wait().
m.s: Updates a key's value with a new value from the specified callback function.

p.s: Key name for which the value should be updated. If DataStoreOptions.AllScopes was set to true when accessing the data store through DataStoreService:GetDataStore(), this key name must be prepended with the original scope as in "scope/key".
Transform function that takes the current value and DataStoreKeyInfo as parameters and returns the new value along with optional UserIds and metadata.

r.s: The updated value of the entry in the data store with the given key and a DataStoreKeyInfo instance that includes the version number, date and time the version was created, and functions to retrieve UserIds and metadata.

kid.simple: The safest way to change saved data. Roblox reads the newest value, passes it to your function, and saves what your function returns. If another server changed it in between, your function runs again with the fresh value. Return nil to cancel.
kid.gotcha: Uses both a read and a write from your budget. Do not wait inside the function.

kid.simple: GlobalDataStore is the basic save box that DataStore and OrderedDataStore are built from. It holds the everyday save functions: get a value, set a value, add to a value, update it safely, and remove it. You use these functions on any data store you get from DataStoreService.
kid.analogy: A GlobalDataStore is like a wall of lockers. Each locker has a label (the key) and something inside (the value). You can look inside, swap what is inside, add to it, or empty it, but each trip to the lockers takes a moment, so you should not run back and forth too often.
whenToUse: Reading saved data with `GetAsync` when a player joins.
Saving data with `SetAsync` or `UpdateAsync` when a player leaves or the server closes.
Counting things across all servers with `IncrementAsync`.
kid.where: Server only. You never create one yourself; get one from `DataStoreService:GetDataStore`, `GetOrderedDataStore` or `GetGlobalDataStore`.

terms.data store: Roblox's save system. It keeps information (like coins or levels) even after players leave and servers shut down, and every server of your game shares it.
terms.key: The name you save a value under, like a label on a locker. A common key is `"User_" .. player.UserId`, for example `User_12345`.
terms.value: The thing stored under a key, like a number, text, true/false, or a table.
terms.server: The Roblox computer in charge of one copy of your game. Data stores can only be used from server Scripts.
terms.pcall: Short for 'protected call'. It runs a function and catches any error instead of letting your whole script crash. It gives back `true` plus the results if it worked, or `false` plus the error message if it failed.
terms.async / yield: Functions ending in `Async` talk to Roblox's computers over the internet, so they take a moment. While waiting, your script pauses (yields), then carries on when the answer arrives.
terms.retry: Trying again after a failure. Data store calls sometimes fail because of the internet, so good code waits a little and tries again a few times.
terms.rate limit / budget: How many data store requests a server is allowed to make per minute. For normal reads and writes the default is 60 + 40 for each player, so a server with 10 players can do 460 reads per minute. If you go over, requests are slowed down or dropped.
terms.throttle: When Roblox slows down or rejects your requests because you sent too many too fast.
terms.UserId: A player's permanent ID number. It never changes, even if they change their name, so it makes a great key.
terms.callback: A function you hand to Roblox so Roblox can run it for you later.
terms.nil: Luau's word for nothing or no value. `GetAsync` returns nil when nothing was ever saved under that key.
terms.version: Every time you save a key, Roblox keeps the old value as an older version for a while, a bit like undo history.
terms.metadata: Extra notes saved alongside a value, like a tag saying when or why it was saved.
terms.cache: A short-term memory. After you read a key, the server remembers it for 4 seconds, and reading again in that time gives the remembered copy.
terms.increment: To add to a number. Incrementing 10 by 5 gives 15. Incrementing by -3 subtracts 3.

examples.title: Save and load coins safely (pcall, retries, PlayerRemoving, BindToClose)
examples.code:
-- Script in ServerScriptService
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local coinStore = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerCoins")

-- Try a data store call up to 5 times, waiting longer each time
local function withRetries(callback)
	local waitTime = 1
	for attempt = 1, 5 do
		local ok, result = pcall(callback) -- catch errors instead of crashing
		if ok then
			return true, result
		end
		warn("Data store attempt " .. attempt .. " failed: " .. tostring(result))
		if attempt < 5 then
			task.wait(waitTime + math.random()) -- small random extra so servers don't all retry together
			waitTime *= 2 -- 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s...
		end
	end
	return false, nil
end

local loaded = {} -- players whose data loaded safely

local function keyFor(player)
	return "User_" .. player.UserId
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	-- Make a leaderboard stat
	local leaderstats = Instance.new("Folder")
	leaderstats.Name = "leaderstats"
	local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
	coins.Name = "Coins"
	coins.Parent = leaderstats
	leaderstats.Parent = player

	-- Load saved coins
	local ok, saved = withRetries(function()
		return coinStore:GetAsync(keyFor(player))
	end)
	if ok then
		coins.Value = saved or 0 -- nil means a brand new player
		loaded[player] = true
	else
		warn("Could not load data for " .. player.Name .. ", will not save to protect it")
	end
end)

local function savePlayer(player)
	if not loaded[player] then
		return -- loading failed, so saving 0 would wipe their real coins
	end
	local leaderstats = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	local coins = leaderstats and leaderstats:FindFirstChild("Coins")
	if not coins then return end
	withRetries(function()
		return coinStore:SetAsync(keyFor(player), coins.Value, { player.UserId })
	end)
end

-- 1. Save when a player leaves
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	savePlayer(player)
	loaded[player] = nil
end)

-- 2. Save everyone when the server shuts down
game:BindToClose(function()
	local stillSaving = 0
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		stillSaving += 1
		task.spawn(function() -- save all players at the same time
			savePlayer(player)
			stillSaving -= 1
		end)
	end
	-- Keep the server alive until every save finishes (Roblox allows up to 30 seconds)
	while stillSaving > 0 do
		task.wait()
	end
end)
explain: `GetDataStore("PlayerCoins")` opens a save box called PlayerCoins. Every server of your game sees the same box.
`withRetries` wraps each call in `pcall`. If Roblox's save servers have a hiccup, the script does not crash; it waits 1 second, then 2, then 4... and tries again, up to 5 times.
When a player joins, we load their coins with `GetAsync`. If nothing was saved yet we get nil, so we start at 0.
If loading failed every time, we remember NOT to save that player. Otherwise we would overwrite their real coins with 0.
`PlayerRemoving` saves the player's coins when they leave.

`game:BindToClose` runs when the server is shutting down (for example, the last player left or you updated the game). Without it, the server could close before saves finish. Roblox waits up to 30 seconds for this function.
Budgets: each server gets about 60 + 40 per player reads and writes per minute. One load per join and one save per leave stays far below that. Do NOT save every time a coin changes.

examples.title: Add to a value safely with UpdateAsync
examples.code:
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerData")

local function addGems(userId, amount)
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		store:UpdateAsync("User_" .. userId, function(oldData)
			oldData = oldData or { Gems = 0 } -- nil for a new player
			oldData.Gems += amount
			return oldData -- returning nil instead would cancel the save
		end)
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("Could not add gems: " .. tostring(err))
	end
end

addGems(12345, 10)
explain: `UpdateAsync` reads the newest saved value, gives it to your function, and saves whatever your function returns.
If another server changed the same key at the same moment, Roblox runs your function again with the newest value, so nothing gets lost.
Returning nil cancels the save.

gotchas: Data stores only work in server Scripts. A LocalScript cannot use them.

In Studio, data stores are off until you publish the game and turn on Game Settings > Security > Enable Studio Access to API Services. Studio uses the same data as the live game, so be careful, or use a separate test place.
Always wrap calls in `pcall`. They talk over the internet and can fail.
Never save in a fast loop or on every coin pickup. You will hit the rate limit. Save on leave, on shutdown, and maybe every few minutes as a backup.
If loading failed, do not save, or you may overwrite good data with empty data.
Keys must be 50 characters or fewer, and one key can hold up to about 4 MB. Text must be valid UTF-8.
Use `player.UserId` in keys, never the player's name (names can change).
You cannot save Instances like Parts or Color3/Vector3 values directly. Save numbers, strings, booleans and plain tables.
`SetAsync` overwrites whatever was there. If two servers might write the same key, use `UpdateAsync`.
The function you give `UpdateAsync` must not wait or yield (no `task.wait` inside); just change the value and return it.

class/GroupService.d:
GroupService is a service that allows developers to fetch information about a Roblox group from within a game.

Basic information on the group, including its name, description, owner, roles and emblem can be fetched using GroupService:GetGroupInfoAsync(). Lists of a group's allies and enemies can be fetched using GroupService:GetAlliesAsync() and GroupService:GetEnemiesAsync().

GroupService can also be used to fetch a list of groups a player is a member of, using GroupService:GetGroupsAsync(). If you wish to verify if a player is in a group, use the Player:IsInGroupAsync() method rather than GroupService:GetGroupsAsync().

The service has a number of useful applications, such as detecting if a player is an ally or enemy upon joining the game, or prompting a player to join a group using the GroupService:PromptJoinAsync() method.

Returns a table describing all roles the specified user holds in the specified group. In a multi-role world, a user may belong to more than one role simultaneously.

The returned table has the following structure:

Key Type Description
IsMember boolean true if the user is a member of the group
Roles array Array of role tables (empty if not a member or no non-base roles)

Each entry in the Roles array has the following structure:

Key Type Description
Id integer Unique role ID
Name string Display name of the role
Rank integer Rank value (0–255)

The Roles array is ordered from the highest role to the lowest role. Only public roles are included. A role's Rank value is retained for backwards compatibility, but does not determine its position in the role hierarchy. Use the stable Id to identify a role.

This method supersedes Player:GetRankInGroupAsync() and Player:GetRoleInGroupAsync(), which return only the member's highest public role.

This call may not yield the most up-to-date information. Results are cached per user and group, so multiple calls with the same userId and groupId may yield the same result until the cache expires. The caching behavior is on a per-peer basis: a server does not share the same cache as a client.

When a player joins a group in-experience due to a call to GroupService:PromptJoinAsync(), any cached result for that player and group will be cleared on the client where the prompt was shown.

PromptJoinAsync() displays a prompt to the local player through which they may join the specified Roblox group. The group must exist and the player must meet the eligibility criteria to join. If the player is ineligible, this method will return GroupMembershipStatus.None.

Note that you can use Player:IsInGroupAsync() to check the player's current membership status before calling this method.

If the player successfully joins, any cached results from GroupService:GetRolesInGroupAsync(), Player:GetRankInGroupAsync(), and Player:GetRoleInGroupAsync() for that player and group will be cleared on the client where the prompt was shown.
m.s: Prompts the local `Class.Player` to join a specified Roblox group via a native modal.

p.s: ID of the group to prompt the player to join. This must be a valid group ID.

r.s: GroupMembershipStatus indicating the player's group membership status after the prompt is closed. If the player closes the prompt without joining, this will return GroupMembershipStatus.None or their previous status if they were already a member.

class/GuiBase.d: GuiBase is an abstract class which most graphical user interface objects inherit from.
class/GuiBase.s: GuiBase is an abstract class which most graphical user interface objects inherit from.

class/GuiBase2d.d: GuiBase2d is an abstract class inherited by 2D GuiObjects.

m.d:
AbsolutePosition is a read-only property that provides the screen position of a GuiBase2d element in pixels. This represents the actual pixel position at which an element renders as a result of its ancestors' sizes and positions. Note that AbsolutePosition always represents the top-left corner of the GuiBase2d element.

If the GuiBase2d is in a ScreenGui, the AbsolutePosition property uses the CoreUISafeInsets viewport coordinate system. The origin of this coordinate system is located at the bottom-left corner of the Roblox top bar. Note that this is the same coordinate system used by the InputObject.Position property.

See also AbsoluteRotation and AbsoluteSize.
m.s: Describes the actual screen position of a `Class.GuiBase2d` element, in pixels.

kid.simple: The real spot on the screen, in pixels, where this UI object's top-left corner ended up. Roblox works it out from the object's Position and all of its parents' sizes and positions. Use it when you need exact pixel numbers, like checking if the mouse is over something.
kid.example:
-- LocalScript inside a Frame
local frame = script.Parent
-- Prints something like 400, 250 (pixels from the top-left of the screen area)
print(frame.AbsolutePosition.X, frame.AbsolutePosition.Y)
kid.gotcha: It is always the TOP-LEFT corner, even if AnchorPoint is (0.5, 0.5). It is read-only, so change Position instead.

m.d:
AbsoluteRotation is a read-only property that describes the actual screen rotation of a GuiBase2d element, in degrees. It does not perform bounds checking, so its value may not be in the range 0 to 360.

See also AbsolutePosition and AbsoluteSize.
m.s: Describes the actual screen rotation of a `Class.GuiBase2d` element, in degrees.

kid.simple: The real angle, in degrees, that this UI object is turned on the screen. It adds up its own Rotation plus any rotation from its parents. A frame turned 10 degrees inside a parent turned 20 degrees has an AbsoluteRotation of 30.
kid.example:
local frame = script.Parent
print("Turned by", frame.AbsoluteRotation, "degrees on screen")
kid.gotcha: It is not kept between 0 and 360, so you might see numbers like 370 or -20.

m.d:
AbsoluteSize is a read-only property that describes the actual screen size of a GuiBase2d element, in pixels.

See also AbsolutePosition and AbsoluteRotation.
m.s: Describes the actual screen size of a `Class.GuiBase2d` element, in pixels.

kid.simple: The real width and height of this UI object, in pixels, after Roblox has done the math. If a frame's Size is 50% of a 1000-pixel-wide screen, its AbsoluteSize.X is 500.
kid.example:
local frame = script.Parent
print("Width:", frame.AbsoluteSize.X, "Height:", frame.AbsoluteSize.Y)
kid.gotcha: It is read-only. It changes when the screen changes size, so don't save it once and assume it stays the same.

m.d:
When set to true, localization will be applied to this GuiBase2d and its descendants. The entries used for localization are the same set of entries returned by LocalizationService:GetTableEntries(). Entries with AutoLocalize enabled are automatically re-translated after the cloud table loads if necessary.

See also RootLocalizationTable.
m.s: When set to `true`, localization will be applied to this `Class.GuiBase2d` and its descendants.

kid.simple: When true (the default), Roblox tries to automatically translate the text in this object and everything inside it into the player's language, using your game's translation tables. Turn it off for text that should never be translated, like a player's name or a score number.
kid.example:
local nameLabel = script.Parent -- a TextLabel that shows a player's name
nameLabel.AutoLocalize = false -- never try to translate names

m.d: This property is automatically set to true when a localization table's LocalizationTable.Root targets this object, or an ancestor of this object. LocalizationTables with their LocalizationTable.Root property pointed at an instance will localize all TextLabel.TextButton that are descendants of the root instance.
m.s: Automatically set to true when a localization table's `Class.LocalizationTable.Root` targets this object, or an ancestor of this object.
m.dep: This item is deprecated. Do not use it for new work.

kid.simple: Old — use AutoLocalize instead.

m.d:
A reference to a LocalizationTable to be used to apply automated localization to this GuiBase2d and its descendants. AutoLocalize must be set to true on the GuiBase2d and its ancestors for automated localization to be applied.

You can set this to reference a LocalizationTable anywhere in the DataModel. The GuiBase2d object and all of its children will try to use that specific LocalizationTable and its ancestors for automatic text replacement before using the tables under LocalizationService in an undefined order and the cloud table.

If there is no translation available in the referenced table, it will look for a translation in the parent of that table, if it is also a LocalizationTable, and so on.

See also LocalizationService:GetTableEntries() which explains how the RootLocalizationTable is used for automated localization.
m.s: A reference to a `Class.LocalizationTable` to be used to apply automated localization to this `Class.GuiBase2d` and its descendants.

kid.simple: Lets you point this UI (and everything inside it) at one specific LocalizationTable (a list of translations) to use first. Only works if AutoLocalize is true on this object and the objects above it. Most games leave it empty and let Roblox use the default tables.
kid.example:
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local screenGui = script.Parent -- a ScreenGui
-- Use this special translation table first for this whole menu
screenGui.RootLocalizationTable = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ShopTranslations")

m.d:
SelectionBehaviorDown customizes how gamepad selection moves in the down direction out of a selection group. It only has an effect when SelectionGroup is true; SelectionGroup is false by default, and while it remains false this property has no effect.

Its default value is SelectionBehavior.Escape, which prioritizes buttons within the selection group but allows the selection to move to a GuiObject outside the group in the down direction if no suitable button is found inside. Setting it to SelectionBehavior.Stop instead constrains the selection to the group, preventing it from moving downward out of the group.

See also SelectionGroup.
m.s: Customizes gamepad selection behavior in the down direction.

kid.simple: Only matters when SelectionGroup is true. Decides what happens when a gamepad player presses down and there is no button below inside this group. Escape (the default) lets the selection leave the group. Stop keeps the selection trapped inside the group.
kid.example:
local menu = script.Parent -- a Frame full of buttons
menu.SelectionGroup = true
menu.SelectionBehaviorDown = Enum.SelectionBehavior.Stop -- can't move down out of the menu

m.d:
SelectionBehaviorLeft customizes how gamepad selection moves in the left direction out of a selection group. It only has an effect when SelectionGroup is true; SelectionGroup is false by default, and while it remains false this property has no effect.

Its default value is SelectionBehavior.Escape, which prioritizes buttons within the selection group but allows the selection to move to a GuiObject outside the group in the left direction if no suitable button is found inside. Setting it to SelectionBehavior.Stop instead constrains the selection to the group, preventing it from moving leftward out of the group.

See also SelectionGroup.
m.s: Customizes gamepad selection behavior in the left direction.

kid.simple: Only matters when SelectionGroup is true. Decides whether gamepad selection can move LEFT out of this group (Escape, the default) or must stay inside (Stop).
kid.example:
local menu = script.Parent
menu.SelectionGroup = true
menu.SelectionBehaviorLeft = Enum.SelectionBehavior.Stop

m.d:
SelectionBehaviorRight customizes how gamepad selection moves in the right direction out of a selection group. It only has an effect when SelectionGroup is true; SelectionGroup is false by default, and while it remains false this property has no effect.

Its default value is SelectionBehavior.Escape, which prioritizes buttons within the selection group but allows the selection to move to a GuiObject outside the group in the right direction if no suitable button is found inside. Setting it to SelectionBehavior.Stop instead constrains the selection to the group, preventing it from moving rightward out of the group.

See also SelectionGroup.
m.s: Customizes gamepad selection behavior in the right direction.

kid.simple: Only matters when SelectionGroup is true. Decides whether gamepad selection can move RIGHT out of this group (Escape, the default) or must stay inside (Stop).
kid.example:
local menu = script.Parent
menu.SelectionGroup = true
menu.SelectionBehaviorRight = Enum.SelectionBehavior.Stop

m.d:
SelectionBehaviorUp customizes how gamepad selection moves in the up direction out of a selection group. It only has an effect when SelectionGroup is true; SelectionGroup is false by default, and while it remains false this property has no effect.

Its default value is SelectionBehavior.Escape, which prioritizes buttons within the selection group but allows the selection to move to a GuiObject outside the group in the up direction if no suitable button is found inside. Setting it to SelectionBehavior.Stop instead constrains the selection to the group, preventing it from moving upward out of the group.

See also SelectionGroup.
m.s: Customizes gamepad selection behavior in the up direction.

kid.simple: Only matters when SelectionGroup is true. Decides whether gamepad selection can move UP out of this group (Escape, the default) or must stay inside (Stop).
kid.example:
local menu = script.Parent
menu.SelectionGroup = true
menu.SelectionBehaviorUp = Enum.SelectionBehavior.Stop

m.d:
Allows for customization of how gamepad selection can move between buttons, which are descendants of the selection group, leave the group, and select other buttons.

Setting SelectionGroup to true exposes the SelectionBehaviorUp, SelectionBehaviorDown, SelectionBehaviorLeft, and SelectionBehaviorRight properties. For these selection behaviors, a setting of SelectionBehavior.Escape (default) means the gamepad selection tries to first find a selection within the selection group and only moves outside if it does not find a suitable button. Alternatively, a setting of SelectionBehavior.Stop means gamepad selection only looks within the selection group and does not move outside of the group from the selection behavior direction.
m.s: Allows customization of gamepad selection movement.

kid.simple: Turns this object into a 'group' for gamepad players. When true, the gamepad selection looks for buttons inside this group first, and the four SelectionBehavior properties decide whether the selection can leave the group. Handy for menus where you don't want the highlight wandering off.
kid.example:
local shopMenu = script.Parent -- a Frame with buttons inside
shopMenu.SelectionGroup = true -- gamepad selection prefers buttons in here
kid.gotcha: The four SelectionBehavior properties do nothing until SelectionGroup is true.

m.d: This event fires when the gamepad selection moves to, leaves, or changes within the connected GuiBase2d or any descendant GuiObjects. When the selection highlight moves to a GuiObject, the event bubbles from that GuiObject to all of its ancestors, informing them that the selection has changed/entered/exited to a GuiObject in their descendant tree.
m.s: Fires when the gamepad selection moves to, leaves, or changes within the connected `Class.GuiBase2d` or any descendant `Class.GuiObject|GuiObjects`.

p.s: True if the new selection matches the attached GuiBase2d.
The GuiObject that was previously selected before the selection changed, or nil if nothing was selected.
The GuiObject that is now selected after the selection changed, or nil if nothing is selected.

kid.simple: Fires when gamepad selection moves onto, off of, or around inside this object or anything inside it. It gives you three things: amISelected (is THIS object the one selected now?), previousSelection, and newSelection.
kid.example:
local menu = script.Parent
menu.SelectionChanged:Connect(function(amISelected, previousSelection, newSelection)
	if newSelection then
		print("Gamepad is now on:", newSelection.Name)
	end
end)

kid.simple: GuiBase2d is the family name for every flat (2D) piece of on-screen stuff in Roblox: frames, buttons, labels, and the containers that hold them like ScreenGui. You never make a GuiBase2d yourself. Instead, every UI thing you make gets its features, like AbsolutePosition and AbsoluteSize, which tell you exactly where it ended up on the screen in pixels.
kid.analogy: GuiBase2d is like the word 'vehicle'. You never buy a 'vehicle', you buy a car or a bike, but every vehicle has wheels and a speed. Every UI object has a real pixel position and size on your screen.
whenToUse: Reading where a UI object really is on the screen in pixels (AbsolutePosition)
Reading how big a UI object really is in pixels (AbsoluteSize)
Turning automatic translation on or off for text (AutoLocalize)
Controlling how gamepad selection moves around a group of buttons (SelectionGroup)
kid.where: Client side. It is a base class, so you cannot do Instance.new("GuiBase2d"). Its properties show up on every UI object (Frame, TextLabel, ScreenGui, and so on). UI code goes in a LocalScript, for example inside StarterGui or StarterPlayerScripts.

terms.base class: A 'parent type' that other types are built from. You can't make one directly, but every type built from it gets its properties.
terms.abstract: Means 'only used as a base class'. You never create it yourself.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on your screen. A typical laptop screen is about 1920 pixels wide and 1080 pixels tall.
terms.absolute: The final, real answer after everything is worked out. AbsoluteSize is the true size in pixels, no matter how the Size was written.
terms.read-only: You can look at the value, but you can't change it from a script. Roblox updates it for you.
terms.Vector2: Two numbers stuck together: X (left-right) and Y (up-down). Example: Vector2.new(400, 250).
terms.descendant: Anything inside an object: its children, their children, and so on, all the way down.
terms.client: The player's own device (their computer, phone, or console). UI lives and runs here.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's device instead of on the Roblox server. All UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.localization: Translating your game's text into other languages, like turning 'Play' into 'Jugar' for Spanish players.
terms.gamepad: A game controller, like an Xbox or PlayStation controller.
terms.deprecated: Old and replaced by something better. It may still work, but you shouldn't use it in new code.

examples.title: Find out where a frame really is on screen
examples.place: LocalScript inside a Frame (inside a ScreenGui in StarterGui)
examples.code:
local frame = script.Parent -- the Frame this LocalScript is inside

-- Size and Position are the 'recipe'. Absolute values are the real result in pixels.
print("Recipe size:", frame.Size)
print("Real size in pixels:", frame.AbsoluteSize)
print("Real top-left corner in pixels:", frame.AbsolutePosition)

-- Absolute values change when the window is resized, so listen for it
frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(function()
	print("New real size:", frame.AbsoluteSize)
end)
explain: script.Parent is the Frame because the LocalScript is placed inside it.
frame.Size is what you typed in (for example 50% of the screen). frame.AbsoluteSize is what that turned into, like (500, 300) pixels on a 1000x600 window.
AbsolutePosition is always the frame's top-left corner in pixels, even if you used AnchorPoint to place it by its center.
GetPropertyChangedSignal runs our function whenever AbsoluteSize changes, for example when the player resizes their window or rotates their phone.

gotchas: Size and Position are what you ask for. AbsoluteSize and AbsolutePosition are what you actually get, in pixels. If your Size uses Scale (percent), the AbsoluteSize changes on every screen size.
AbsolutePosition is always the top-left corner, not the AnchorPoint. A centered frame still reports its top-left corner.
You can't set AbsolutePosition or AbsoluteSize. To move or resize something, change Position or Size instead.
Inside a ScreenGui, AbsolutePosition is measured from just below the Roblox top bar (unless the ScreenGui ignores that inset), so (0, 0) may not be the very top pixel of the window.

m.s: Sets the color of this `Class.GuiBase3d` object.
